detail:
StatPearls' small fiber neuropathy chapter describes a disorder of the small-diameter nerve fibers: thinly myelinated A-delta fibers and unmyelinated C fibers, which mediate pain, thermal sensation, and autonomic function. Typical symptoms are burning pain, tingling, and sensitivity that often begin in the feet and follow a stocking-glove distribution, sometimes with autonomic features such as abnormal sweating or blood pressure changes.

The chapter emphasizes why the condition is missed: nerve conduction studies test large fibers and are normal in isolated small fiber neuropathy. The key confirmatory test is a skin punch biopsy measuring intraepidermal nerve fiber density, reported at about 88% sensitivity, with autonomic tests such as QSART as adjuncts. Diabetes is the most common identifiable cause; in many people no cause is found.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about evaluation for unexplained burning pain.
summary: StatPearls explains that small fiber neuropathy damages the thin A-delta and C nerve fibers that carry pain, temperature, and autonomic signals, causing burning pain and sensitivity, often in a stocking-glove pattern, while standard nerve conduction studies stay normal.
takeaways: burning pain and temperature sensitivity are hallmark symptoms
normal nerve conduction studies do not rule it out
a skin punch biopsy measuring nerve fiber density is the key test
autonomic symptoms like sweating changes can occur
title: Small fiber neuropathy: pain the usual nerve tests miss
